description: Browser realtime-audio app — WebAudio mic capture, FFT visualization, WebRTC peer-audio stub.

defaults.headline: Starter Foundry Realtime Audio
defaults.subheadline: Mic capture, FFT visualization, and a WebRTC peer-audio seam — browser-native.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick realtime-audio-ts when the app captures microphone audio in the browser, visualizes it with an AnalyserNode / FFT, and optionally streams it to a peer via WebRTC. If the user wants voice chat with server-mediated rooms, use a signalling-server + this template — the peer.ts stub has the RTCPeerConnection wired and documents where to plug in the signalling transport.
architectureNotes: src/audio.ts owns the AudioContext lifecycle — it is created lazily on the first user gesture to satisfy autoplay policy (Chrome/Safari refuse to run an AudioContext started before a click).
src/visualizer.ts runs a requestAnimationFrame loop that reads from AnalyserNode.getByteFrequencyData into a preallocated Uint8Array (allocating in the RAF loop causes GC jank at 60fps).

src/peer.ts is an RTCPeerConnection harness that accepts an inbound MediaStream, adds its tracks to the peer connection, and exposes createOffer/applyAnswer hooks. Signalling is OUT OF SCOPE — the stub documents exactly where to wire a WebSocket/Ably/Pusher transport.
src/main.ts is the glue: Start button → requestUserMedia → audio.start(stream) → visualizer.attach(analyser) → peer.addLocalStream(stream).
components: Start/Stop button that unlocks the AudioContext on click.
Canvas-based FFT bar visualizer (one draw per RAF tick).
Mute / gain slider wired through a GainNode.
Signalling transport seam — a comment block in peer.ts marks where WebSocket code goes.
gotchas: AUTOPLAY POLICY: a freshly-created AudioContext is suspended in Chrome, Safari, and Firefox until a user gesture. Call audioContext.resume() inside the click handler — NOT at module load — or getByteFrequencyData returns all zeros with no error.
getUserMedia requires HTTPS (or localhost). On any other http:// origin the browser silently blocks the prompt. Use `vite --host 0.0.0.0 --https` for LAN testing.

Safari: audioContext.sampleRate differs from Chrome/Firefox (defaults to 44100 or device rate). If you hardcode 48000 in any FFT math the visualizer shifts on Safari — always read `audioContext.sampleRate`.
Allocating Uint8Array inside the RAF loop causes GC pauses. Preallocate ONE array at attach time and reuse it every frame.
AnalyserNode.fftSize must be a power of 2 between 32 and 32768. Set it once at creation; changing it mid-stream is allowed but reallocates buffers internally and glitches the canvas.
RTCPeerConnection: you MUST call addTrack for each track BEFORE createOffer, otherwise the SDP has no m=audio section and the remote peer won't know you're sending audio.
iOS Safari: AudioContext is destroyed when the page goes to the background for >30s. Listen to visibilitychange and resume() on return, or the meters freeze permanently.

Echo cancellation: set `{ echoCancellation: true, noiseSuppression: true, autoGainControl: true }` in getUserMedia constraints — defaults vary by browser and you'll get feedback loops in P2P audio without these.
ICE servers: the peer stub uses Google's public STUN by default. For production you need TURN servers — without them, symmetric-NAT clients fail to connect ~20% of the time.
integrations: Web Audio API (native) — AudioContext, AnalyserNode, GainNode
Bring-your-own signalling transport (WebSocket / Ably / Pusher / socket.io)
